transcript: so about four months ago I started writing a play I wasn't intending to write a play but then this idea hit me and I'm like this could this could be something and then it became a play and first it was a one act play and then I shared it with a good friend who knows things and was like this needs a second act and that's when things got weird so in a nutshell the play is highly personal it's about moving in with my mother it's about multi generational household it's about it's about a crisis that happens and what happens when a bunch of people from different backgrounds have to get together and hunker down when something's happening and then what happens when that thing that we were hunkering down for isn't exactly what we expected some of the themes I try to explore are caregiving through grief political polarization memory and perception secrets and confrontation um there's a lot in there and um again I'm not sure if it's successful but it's it's what I did I've shared the play with a handful of trusted friends and I can tell some of them are like just encouraging me to keep going you know great keep going some of them just were perplexed and some really really liked it like they weren't blowing smoke like they told me it was really good and I was like really cause I just don't know sometimes you just feel like you know you're smelling your own farts as they say so I have to kind of spinning around in circles with like what to do with this thing cause I wrote it I felt accomplished but I'm like I wanna see if this has legs um and I looked at various theatre companies in my area in southern southern suburbs of Chicago and there are groups and theatre communities that have like playwriting development courses I just couldn't make it work with my schedule um and it required several meetings to kind of get into like the crux of what you written so I was like I guess I'm I'm impatient in one degree and then I had a friend that wanted to like develop it into a play while I doing a workshop in New York and it just wasn't it was too it was becoming too big for me as someone who's like a um a new playwright I just felt like I didn't trust that it was ready for that level and I don't think my ego was ready for something that big I needed something that was contained smaller and felt safer and felt like I could like learn from this experience versus like go full out with something and again I'm not even sure if it's any good well then I stumbled upon a theatre group through this app Anaconda Theatre Ensemble based in Anaconda um Montana um and Jackie who is the founder of that theatre company reached out to me and said hey I'd love to read your play I help develop new plays we kinda this is what we do as a theatre company and so I shared it with her and she was very encouraging about it and she said listen let's try something so they're doing kind of a test of like this new concept they've tried it once before but not in this fashion we're doing a virtual closed read of it this weekend where she has secured some outstanding local actors to read it in the virtual session with some trusted people to come and observe that reading and then provide feedback after either in a form that we've developed with some pointed questions or some people have been invited to stay and have like a talk back and um it's happening this weekend I'm really excited and nervous about it um and I'll let you know how it goes but I think that this is such a cool concept to have people who especially in areas like Montana who don't have access to theatre opportunities and they can do something like this and perform and have the ability to create something new whether it's good or bad I don't know but it gives me an opportunity to participate in the creation of something um despite the proximity to being able to do it in a physical location so I'm really looking forward to how this goes and um I'll share how afterwards maybe I'll just I'll just throw my hands up and say I'm never doing this again but um I'm putting myself out there which I'm really proud that I've done this and I really appreciate Jackie and Anaconda Theatre Ensemble which I've tagged in the comments below for helping with this and they are also always looking for submissions they have a submission window for new plays so they're gonna see kinda how this process goes with this kind of virtual reading workshop and tweak it and um so if you have something that you're interested in having developed they're a great um company to consider
